scope: NCollection_UBTree::Clear explicit preorder payload destruction and optional allocator replacement over the existing arena facade
source_scope: UBTree/EBTree/filler source, shared destruction guards, selected tests and native probes; not complete compiler/allocator dependency closure.

method_bindings.domain: Explicit clearing of a valid checked tree: root, child zero, child one preorder; object before bounds; retain old allocator unless a nonnull replacement was requested and cleanup completes.
Payload destruction order only. Individual arena node deallocation differs from native deferred paired-array frees.

behavior: Clear no longer delegates live payload destruction to Vec insertion order. It walks the live root graph in native preorder and destroys each object before its bounds at its original allocation address.

Kill and Clear share a focused destruction module with the existing NativeNodeOwner allocation guard and DeferredDestructorPanic. No new unsafe code, public method bounds, generic Drop implementation or public field changes are introduced.

Clear releases original typed allocator allocations and incremental live leases before adopting a requested allocator. An empty Clear may still adopt a replacement; no replacement preserves identity. Subsequent insertion starts at arena index zero using the selected allocator.

If a Rust destructor panics, Clear drains remaining payloads and deallocates their slots, empties root/last/arena metadata, retains the original allocator and resumes the first panic. Reuse after catching that panic is tested. This is a Rust safety extension, not native throwing-destructor parity.

Safe public mutable-node replacement and clone_from can detach descendants or copy cyclic, duplicate or foreign child identifiers. Traversal skips absent or previously released identifiers, then drains remaining arena-owned slots in index order. This preserves ownership and termination for that existing safe API domain without claiming a native malformed-graph oracle.

Native callbacks observe the original allocator and nonnull root during destruction; replacement and root-null publication occur afterwards. Rust detaches checked root/last before destruction to preserve safe panic recovery and has no public safe reentrant tree observer. That observer-state difference remains explicitly open.

Native Kill and Clear probes now share one small trace header. Previously committed receipt hashes and archived source snapshots remain unchanged; all prior native output rows were rerun unchanged after this fixture-only extraction.

compatibility.baseline_actual_library_probe: Restored exact branch-base ubtree.rs and ubtree/removal.rs, built the actual TKernel rlib, compiled and ran the probe; exit0. The new destruction module is unreferenced in this baseline.
compatibility.candidate_actual_library_probe: Restored final production files, rebuilt actual TKernel rlib, compiled and ran the identical probe; exit0. Final selected tests/Miri subsequently use those same sources.
compatibility.probe_domain: Late-declared referents accepted by BoundingNode and ObjBnd drop-check; public field partial moves; ordinary UBTree borrowed str payload insertion/clear; UBTree key covariance and Send/Sync/Unpin/UnwindSafe/RefUnwindSafe positive bounds.
compatibility.evidence: Exact baseline source files, compile/run command script, build logs and probe source are archived. Existing payload compatibility tests also run unchanged in normal/Miri sweeps.

remaining_gaps: Gemmate still allocates separate arena nodes and clones instead of native paired allocation/default construction/member assignment. Clear and Kill release each individual allocation during traversal; native delNode defers child-pair frees until payload traversal completes, then Clear frees the root. No allocation count, byte layout or pair-free timing parity is credited.

Automatic UBTree destruction and move-assignment destruction still use implicit arena owner drops. This slice changes explicit Clear and its callers only; no generic Drop implementation is added because borrowed drop-check compatibility requires a separate ownership design.

Native destructor-body child-pointer clearing, raw Child/Parent pointer projections and native reentrant observer root/last state are still absent. Rust checked last state becomes None; native Clear leaves a dangling last pointer.
Moved-from allocator null state, filler equal-slot assignment effects, borrowed filler insertion and generic address-sensitive construction remain as prior receipts describe.

Malformed or disconnected checked graphs and Rust destructor-panic recovery are safety extensions, not native parity claims. Simultaneously panicking object and bounds destructors within one node remain subject to Rust double-panic termination.
Global API/declaration coverage is unchanged. These local callable-method contracts do not establish complete UBTree, TreeNode or UBTreeFiller parity.
